## formal
In the jet algebra of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.field-level-brst-differential-of-the-derived-gauge-fields-is-nilpotent}, with the gauge algebra $\su(2) \oplus \su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} realised there by bivectors ($T_{1}, T_{2}, T_{3} = \tfrac12e_{12}, \tfrac12e_{20}, \tfrac12e_{01}$ in $\Cl(3,0)$ on $e_{0}, e_{1}, e_{2}$, colour on $e_{3}, \dots, e_{8}$, $T_{12} = \tfrac12J$), the structure constants $f_{ab}{}^{c}$ and the invariant form $\kappa_{ab} = -\langle T_{a}T_{b}\rangle_{0}$, add the two doublets of the scalar sector: each is an even element $\phi = \phi^{0} + \phi^{1}e_{12} + \phi^{2}e_{02} + \phi^{3}e_{01}$ of $\Cl(3,0)$, with $\rho(T_{a})\phi = T_{a}\phi$ ($a = 1, 2, 3$), colour acting by $0$, and $\rho(T_{12})\phi = y\,\phi e_{12}$ for a rational $y \ne 0$ (the normalisation of hypercharge); $\langle\phi, \psi\rangle = \langle\widetilde{\phi}\psi\rangle_{0}$. Write $\phi = v + h$ with $v$ constant (the vacuum) and $h = (h^{1}, \dots, h^{8})$ even jet symbols, $\rho(c) = c^{a}\rho(T_{a})$, $D_\mu\phi = \partial_\mu h + g\rho(A^{a}_{\mu}T_{a})\phi$, $W_{a} = \rho(T_{a})v$ and $\Gamma_{ab} = \langle W_{a}, W_{b}\rangle$. Extend the stored differential by
\[
sh = -g\,\rho(c)(v + h), \qquad s(h_{J}) = \partial_{J}(sh).
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The doublets; proved.)} $\rho$ is a representation of the twelve generators by maps antisymmetric for $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$, for every $y$; with hypercharge acting on the left it is not.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Nilpotency; proved.)} $s^{2} = 0$ on the whole jet algebra, for every constant $v$, every $y$ and every $g$; with $sh = +g\rho(c)(v + h)$ it fails.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Invariance; proved.)} $s(D_\mu\phi) = -g\rho(c)D_\mu\phi$; $s$ annihilates $\tfrac12\langle D_\mu\phi, D^{\mu}\phi\rangle$ and every polynomial in $|\phi_{1}|^{2}$, $|\phi_{2}|^{2}$, $\langle\phi_{1}, \phi_{2}\rangle$, $\langle\phi_{1}, \phi_{2}e_{12}\rangle$, so with the stored Yang-Mills density in the canonical normalisation, $\mathcal{L} = \tfrac12\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_{0} + \tfrac12\langle D_\mu\phi, D^{\mu}\phi\rangle - V$ is $s$-invariant for every such $V$ ($\tfrac12\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_{0} = -\tfrac14F^{a}_{\mu\nu}F^{b\,\mu\nu}$).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The 't Hooft gauge; proved.)} For $\Psi_{\xi} = \kappa_{ab}\bar c^{a}\big(\nabla\cdot A^{b} + \tfrac{\xi}{2}B^{b}\big) - \xi g\,\bar c^{a}\langle W_{a}, h\rangle$, with $F^{a} = \nabla\cdot A^{a} - \xi g\,\kappa^{ab}\langle W_{b}, h\rangle$,
\[
s\Psi_{\xi} = \kappa_{ab}B^{a}F^{b} + \tfrac{\xi}{2}\kappa_{ab}B^{a}B^{b} - \kappa_{ab}\bar c^{a}\,\nabla\cdot(Dc)^{b} - \xi g^{2}\,\bar c^{a}\langle W_{a}, \rho(c)(v + h)\rangle, \qquad s(s\Psi_{\xi}) = 0,
\]
and after eliminating $B$ ($B^{a} = -F^{a}/\xi$, giving $-\tfrac{1}{2\xi}\kappa_{ab}F^{a}F^{b}$) the terms of $\tfrac12\langle D_\mu\phi, D^{\mu}\phi\rangle - \tfrac{1}{2\xi}\kappa_{ab}F^{a}F^{b}$ bilinear in $A$ and $h$ are exactly $g\,\partial_\mu\big(A^{a\mu}\langle W_{a}, h\rangle\big)$, a total derivative, for every $v$ and $\xi$; with the opposite sign of the 't Hooft term they are not a total derivative.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Masses; proved, computed.)} With the normalisation of (iii), the vector quadratic form at $\xi = 1$ is $-\tfrac12\kappa_{ab}\,\partial_\mu A^{a}_{\nu}\partial^{\mu}A^{b\nu}$ up to a total derivative (Feynman type; with the density $\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_{0}$ this happens at $\xi = \tfrac12$ instead). Suppose $V = 0$, or $v$ is a stationary point of the invariant potential $V$; then $\mathrm{Hess}\,V(v)$ annihilates every $W_{a}$ (differentiate $\langle\nabla V(\phi), \rho(T_{a})\phi\rangle = 0$ at $v$), and off a stationary point there is a tadpole. Under this hypothesis the squared masses of the vectors, the ghosts and the Goldstone modes are the eigenvalues of $g^{2}\kappa^{-1}\Gamma$, $\xi g^{2}\kappa^{-1}\Gamma$ and $\xi g^{2}W\kappa^{-1}W^{\mathsf T}$ (on the eight scalars), the potential adding nothing on the Goldstone directions; the nonzero ones agree with multiplicity, so at $\xi = 1$ every massive vector, its Goldstone mode and its ghosts share one mass. For the neutral aligned vacuum $v = (v_{1}, 0, 0, 0), (v_{2}, 0, 0, 0)$ (Goldstone rank $3$, as stored), the nonzero eigenvalues of $\kappa^{-1}\Gamma$ equal to $v_{1}^{2} + v_{2}^{2}$ (twice) and $(v_{1}^{2} + v_{2}^{2})(1 + \tfrac43y^{2})$; computed at $v_{1} = 1$, $v_{2} = 2$, $y = \tfrac12$: $\det(t - \kappa^{-1}\Gamma) = t^{9}(t - 5)^{2}(t - \tfrac{20}{3})$ and $\det(t - W\kappa^{-1}W^{\mathsf T}) = t^{5}(t - 5)^{2}(t - \tfrac{20}{3})$, the factor $t^{5}$ counting five massless scalars only for $V = 0$ (a potential gives the five non-Goldstone scalars their own masses).
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Computed.)} (i) for $y = \tfrac12, \tfrac13$; (ii) on the $40$ generators $h^{i}_{J}$ with $|J| \le 1$ and the $72$ underived gauge, ghost and antighost generators, as polynomials in $g$ and eight formal vacuum components; (iii) on all $32$ components of $D\phi$, the kinetic term and the four invariants, with two non-invariant bilinears as controls; (iv) term by term, $256$ mixing monomials at $\xi = 1, 3$; (v) from the computed Lagrangian, the Feynman form of the vector kinetic term at $\xi = 1$ by Euler derivatives (and its failure for the unhalved density, which is of Feynman type at $\xi = \tfrac12$), and for a sample invariant potential stationary at the neutral aligned vacuum the vanishing gradient and the Hessian annihilating the three Goldstone directions (a shifted potential has a tadpole).
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} With the differential extended to the scalar sector (nilpotent for every vacuum, the lemma (ii)), the 't Hooft-Feynman gauge with the series' two doublets is an exact gauge fixing in which the vector-Goldstone mixing cancels and the vectors, Goldstone modes and ghosts share their masses, the gauge in which the stored quartet result treats the massive vectors. The vacuum, and hence the breaking pattern, is an input here.

## technical
The stored field-level BRST differential of the derived gauge fields left out the scalars. Here the series' two hypercharge-$\tfrac12$ doublets are written as even elements of $\Cl(3,0)$, with the weak bivectors acting on the left and hypercharge by a multiple of $e_{12}$ on the right, so the gauge algebra acts by real antisymmetric maps and no imaginary unit appears. The differential $sh = -g\rho(c)(v + h)$ around any constant vacuum $v$ squares to zero on all fields, the covariant derivative transforms covariantly, and the kinetic term and the four quadratic invariants of two doublets are BRST-invariant. The 't Hooft gauge-fixing fermion, which adds $-\xi g\,\bar c^{a}\langle\rho(T_{a})v, h\rangle$ to the covariant one, is exact, and its gauge-fixing function cancels the mixing between vectors and Goldstone modes up to a total derivative for every vacuum. In the Feynman-'t Hooft gauge, with the canonical normalisation of the Yang-Mills term and a vacuum that is a stationary point of the potential, the massive vectors, their Goldstone modes and their ghosts have one common mass matrix; for the neutral aligned vacuum the Goldstone map has rank three, as stored.

## lay
In the series' version of the Standard Model, the forces have a mathematical bookkeeping device, BRST symmetry, that makes their quantum theory consistent; it had been written down for the force fields alone. Here it is extended to the two Higgs-like scalar fields of the series, written in geometric algebra as four-component quantities on which the weak force acts from one side and hypercharge from the other. The extended symmetry is consistent whatever value the scalars settle at, and in the standard gauge choice due to 't Hooft the unwanted mixing between the force fields and the would-be Goldstone particles cancels, while the massive force carriers, their Goldstone partners and the bookkeeping ghost fields all share the same masses. Which way the symmetry breaks is not decided here; it is put in by hand.

## one-liner
With the two doublets as even elements of $\Cl(3,0)$ (weak bivectors on the left, hypercharge $y\,e_{12}$ on the right), $sh = -g\rho(c)(v + h)$ extends the stored differential nilpotently for every vacuum; the 't Hooft fermion $\kappa\bar c(\nabla\cdot A + \tfrac{\xi}{2}B) - \xi g\bar c^{a}\langle\rho(T_{a})v, h\rangle$ is exact, cancels the vector-Goldstone mixing up to a total derivative, and at $\xi = 1$, with the canonical $\tfrac12\kappa\langle FF\rangle_{0}$ and at a stationary vacuum, gives vectors, Goldstones and ghosts one mass matrix (rank $3$ for the neutral aligned vacuum).
